speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are experiencing progressive difficulty walking, urinary incontinence, and speech difficulties. To begin my assessment, how long have these symptoms been present, and did they start suddenly or gradually?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing a gradual difficulty in walking over the past 3 months, requiring wheelchair assistance for the last month. Additionally, there is a history of urinary incontinence for 1 year and recent onset of speech slurring making communication challenging.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Multiple Sclerosis.

The patient is a 54-year-old male with a 3-month history of progressive gait difficulty worsening to wheelchair dependence, 1-year history of urinary incontinence, and recent onset of speech slurring. These symptoms suggest a progressive demyelinating condition affecting multiple neurological regions. Before confirming the diagnosis, I will request an MRI of the brain and spine to look for characteristic white matter lesions.

REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain and Spine with and without contrast.

REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain and Spine with and without contrast.
